message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, known for their high passenger traffic, extensive flight networks, and significant economic impact:

| Airport | City | State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|------|-------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport | Atlanta | Georgia | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport | Los Angeles | California | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and Latin America; busiest airport on the West Coast. |
| O'Hare International Airport | Chicago | Illinois | ORD | One of the oldest major hubs; key connecting point for domestic and international flights. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport | Dallas/Fort Worth | Texas | DFW | Largest airport in the U.S. by land area; major hub for American Airlines. |
| Denver International Airport | Denver | Colorado | DEN | Largest airport by land area in the U.S.; major hub for United Airlines and Southwest. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport | New York City | New York | JFK | Major gateway to Europe and the Caribbean; hub for many international carriers. |
| San Francisco International Airport | San Francisco | California | SFO | Major hub for United Airlines; key gateway to Asia and the Pacific Rim. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport | Seattle | Washington | SEA | Hub for Alaska Airlines and a major gateway to Asia. |
| Miami International Airport | Miami | Florida | MIA | Major hub for international flights to Latin America and the Caribbean. |
| Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport | Phoenix | Arizona | PHX | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the busiest airports in the Southwest. |
| Charlotte Douglas International Airport | Charlotte | North Carolina | CLT | Major hub for American Airlines; one of the fastest-growing airports in the U.S. |
| Newark Liberty International Airport | Newark | New Jersey | EWR | Major hub for United Airlines; key gateway to Europe and the Caribbean. |
| Washington Dulles International Airport | Washington, D.C. | Virginia | IAD | Major hub for United Airlines; key gateway to Europe and the Middle East. |
| Orlando International Airport | Orlando | Florida | MCO | Major hub for domestic travel and tourism; hub for Southwest Airlines. |

These airports serve as critical hubs for both domestic and international travel, and they play a vital role in the U.S. economy and global connectivity.
